card.name: Manner words ending a verb phrase
card.fires_on: The final word of a manner phrase after a verb or noun, such as "way" after an adjective, or an adverb ending like -ly, -ably, -ently. It sits where the phrase says how something is done.

modes.label: "way" after an adjective
modes.description: The word "way" closes a phrase describing manner, such as cost-effective way or negative way.
modes.example: Handling manure from his hog feeding platforms and cattle yards in a cost-effective<< way>> wouldn’t normally be considered an easy task

modes.label: Adverb endings
modes.description: The -ly or -ably ending of a manner adverb that finishes a clause.
modes.example: governments (national and sub-national) must treat overseas tenders no less favour<<ably>> than local ones

modes.label: Adverb after a verb
modes.description: A full adverb such as closely or positively right after a verb or object.
modes.example: Monitor patients<< closely>>, especially within the first 24

card.writes: It seems to push toward word endings and tokens that finish a manner phrase, not clearly toward any specific word.
card.plain: It lights up on the last word of a phrase saying how something is done, like "in a negative way" or "monitor closely".
